Representative_Docs: ["So as a result of that, I'm going to be focused on the strategy part of our business in my comments today and walk through what we view as the long-term opportunity in agriculture and how we, as a company, fit into that. Most conversations here in the recent few weeks about agriculture and about [COMPANY] begin with a conversation about the volatility of commodity prices and the ability for us as a company to grow in this environment. Innovation is really what differentiates us as a company and allows us to be a growth company through what we see as volatile commodity price cycles. Our confidence in being able to grow via that innovation comes from looking back, frankly, over the last couple of decades, there are some periods where we've seen a lot of volatility in the ag cycle. And if you look at those periods, it's been some of our most rapid growth as a company driven by the adoption of the technologies that we invented. If you look to the more recently, in the last 5 years, we've seen our business grow aggressively through the adoption of the Roundup Ready 2 Yield soybean platform, as well as our reduced refuge family in corn during this time, which really, again, continued our growth approach. So these are great examples of us being able to grow our business and having farmers adopt technologies that improve their yield and productivity in all types of commodity cycles. So at the end of the day, our view is about investment in R&D and turning that investment into new technologies that help drive a farmer's productivity, whether it be yield or cost reduction on the farm. And as I look forward to our business, I see a business here that we have today that's more global than it's ever been. And that would give us confidence that we will continue to grow as we look forward through various commodity cycles that we're going to see in agriculture and gives us confidence in our 5-year growth plan. I'd like to spend a few minutes just talking about the case that we are in a robust demand cycle and continue to be in agriculture. And it's really driven by demand-driven runway that exists in agriculture broadly. Structurally, we believe that these last few months does not define the long-term runway in agriculture. There's good fundamental strong demand curve. If you agree with -- our view that in the next 5 years and beyond, we're really going to have to deliver most of that yield by adding yield per acre versus new acres, given the constraints on the ability to add new acres globally. There's going to be a demand for technology and know-how and solutions on the farm that can meet those demand prospects and productivity prospects. And that's why we're relevant because what we do -- at the heart of what we do is innovate technologies and products that help a farmer drive that productivity on a per acre basis. So as we look at the next 5 years, we really see this as the intersection of the demand curves I just talked about and the innovation that differentiates us. Put very simply, the products and technologies that we have in place today, there's clearly a market opportunity for these because we are focused around yield and productivity. And that's what gives us confidence in our growth plan over the next 5 years to more than double our earnings that we -- the plan and the target that we laid out in June to do that by 2019. The biggest driver of our ability to double our earnings during this period of time is our core business, our core seeds and traits business. A lot of this is the continuation of factors that we're known for, such as our breeding capability across crops, as well as the ability to expand our corn germplasm franchise and trait footprint. And then you layer on top of that the transformational power of some of the new platforms that [PERSON] talked about towards the end of this period, not only adds some additional growth towards the end, but really sets us up for the trends in the next decade. So let's look a little more detail in at the growth plan of at least doubling our EPS through 2019. And there's, as I said, more than $4 billion of gross profit growth from our seeds and traits business that really drives this doubling. As I said, there's 3 $1 billion-plus opportunities that contribute across corn and soybeans. The first I'll go through is, again, what we call the decade of soybean. Let's start then with the driver that creates the biggest new increment of growth, and that's our soybean platform. This technology is a definite yield and a farm productivity story. This is a technology that's revolutionary in the new yield and value it creates, and we're hearing that loud and clear from our grower customers. We've got some near-term data points to verify that. We're seeing in that northern part of Argentina, where we have close relationship with a set of growers there, good intentions there as we talk to those growers and visit with our retailers who service those customers. So really good confidence that this 2015 year and that 10 million to 12 million acres is a great runway as we project out over the next 5 years. The second platform then that's right behind Intacta is Roundup Ready Xtend. Today, we have more than 90% of the seed companies who service the U.S. market licensed on this platform, and we expect to have a similar outcome as we think about taking this platform to South America towards the end of the decade. One is the total opportunity for this technology platform. And we think this technology has a fit on a significant portion of these acres. There's an opportunity and need, frankly, to step up production not only in developed markets, but emerging markets as well, which create new opportunity for us. There's still areas where we have upgrade traits like South America, as well as potential new markets like Canada where we can grow corn for the first time and have traits there. So it's a great example of why we are confident in our growth prospects. We've talked a lot about so far the macro trends that really set a compelling runway to agriculture and the catalysts that exists within our core business as our seeds and traits business to drive the opportunity in the next 5 years. Bottom line, we think the grower is going to need more and more new technologies to deliver the more yields that the world's going to demand. So let me talk just a few minutes towards the end here about our new platforms and which we view frankly as virtually untapped opportunities that are in front of us. I'll start with our biologicals opportunity. Today, if you look at the biological microbial area, it's a $2.5-ish billion business that's growing at 25% -- 20% to 25% growth rate, so real -- a real opportunity here in front of us. Let's shift to the second new platform, precision agriculture. And the final point I'd make, and this is at the core and the heart of what The Climate Corporation does is starts to understand and be able to understand the impact of weather, which is the single most variable factor that impacts agriculture today and helps them manage that variability to make better decisions within it. So in closing, I'll just summarize our discussion with the following key points: One, the opportunity in agriculture is significant given the long-term underlying demand factors. Two, going forward, most of that new demand is going to have to be met by improving productivity per acre, not new acres. And then the final point is companies who can deliver that new yield and productivity, there's going to be tremendous opportunity. That's what we lead in, it's that innovation that drives productivity. But as importantly, we have the opportunity to create the next major transformation in agriculture with biologicals and our precision ag platform. As farmers become more digitized, we see the underlying power of data and information to be literally the integrator of a lot of decisions and inputs that go onto the farm. And for us, that means it's a gateway into a billion-acre-plus opportunity to reach into many of those 40 decisions that a farmer makes on every field, every crop, every year and really extend that beyond our corn crops and geographies.", "So I'm going to jump right into it and talk about the North American season, and how that's shaping up and then what are the factors that are driving our growth and how we're tracking on that. So from a competitive perspective, from a marketplace perspective, what drives our earnings and accounts for the '14 growth, and then I'll a project a little bit longer because I really think they really lay out the runway for our sustainable growth for the future. A couple of points I'll just highlight and emphasize that our growth is clearly driven by our seed technology. Certainly, there's a bit of volatility and a lot of conversation in the ag space around commodity prices and acres and currency, but we're very confident that our growth is on track and that we will deliver the year. And I think that's important because that really sets the tone for our continued growth and how we build on that growth with some of the new areas we're in, both via the biologicals and the precision ag. And I'll just step back and talk a little bit about the long-term trends because I think they are so critical. If you fast-forward and you think about the next 10 years, and we've taken a pretty conservative view in our modeling. And of course, that's driven by continued increase in population, income, protein demand. And the important point is, as we look into the future, most of that demand is not going to be met by incremental acres. But the majority of this demand is going to be met by higher productivity, and that's key. And that's a high level of productivity, that's higher than what we've seen traditionally, but I think the important point is with the technology and tools that are available, I think it's really achievable. And I think the bottom line from all this, the case I'd make is that if you look at the long-term, agriculture is a great business to be in and it's particularly a good place if you're a technology provider that's driving that innovation opportunity in the marketplace. So if I overlay that brief look at the demand scenario over our business, I think we're at a pretty important inflection point where more technology than ever is going to be needed to deliver the yield and productivity. But I can tell you that based on our North American season and the early data points, that we're progressing well, we are on track to deliver the business objectives that we've outlined and we have a high degree of confidence in the factors that will drive our growth. We've-- in that's -- in a world where acres in Latin America have contracted, where there's fewer acres in the U.S., we've seen expansion of corn acres in Eastern Europe, and we're tracking well there. The second point I'd emphasize is last couple of years have been very tough production years. The COGS improvement will be significant for our corn business and we're seeing that play out. From a soybean perspective, the big news is the launch of our Intacta product in Latin America. The overall launch of over 3 million acres was the largest launch we've had for a soybean product. A couple of the other things I would highlight is that beyond the seed businesses, we're making a great progress in launching a couple of 2 new platforms for the company. We're very excited to have that transaction complete and we're excited about the BioAg Alliance, a tremendous opportunity to use new tools and technology to understand that microplant interaction, ability to use the same types of genetic tools and testing capability that we use for our seeds and deliver products that could enhance yield and crop performance. So let me jump in and talk specifically on the commodity price side and talk about the bridge that between our near-term focus and that longer-term opportunity that I highlighted earlier. And so what I'd emphasize here is our business model has always been about delivering better-performing, higher-yielding products. And we've done that year in and year out, and it's that constant upgrade of new genetics and new traits that really drives the pricing opportunity in our portfolio. And the last thing I'd highlight is that a big part of this is the upgrade that we see in our genetics, and that's really what drives that 5% to 10% lift. And that's really -- it gets down to the heart of why the technology story is so important, and it's that breeding engine that drives that next-generation, better performing hybrid of that better trait package that moves us as a business. We're the largest crop breeder in the world and it's that capability that differentiates us competitively. And we tie that to our gene discovery capabilities and using the markers and the breeding tools to change breeding using the ability to understand every gene in the corn plant to be able to map and tag those genes, to be able to create new combinations and really identify more quickly where we can optimize yield and performance and then tying that to our testing network. Our target is to replace about 20% or 25% of the corn hybrids with the soybean varieties in every major market every year, and that's what creates a big part of the mix price lift that we have. And that's -- one of the aspects of our business that I think is probably the least understood is there's a lot of focus, typically, on the U.S. and Brazil, but the expansion of these markets internationally is quite significant. And that's why despite the reduced acres in the U.S. and South America, we are actually going to have a record year for our global corn volume sales this year. It's the combination of great soils, good agricultural systems and a climate and an environment that is conducive to growing corn. Effectively, what's going to happen, I think, in the Ukraine and Russia over the next several years is a lot of those wheat acres that are being used today for feed production will convert to corn. We won't convert all of that, but I think a big portion of that could be an opportunity for growth in the future. And so we've geared our breeding programs to produce the shortest season hybrids that will be important for that market. Our market share in Ukraine, for example, is between 20% and 25% without having really the targeted breeding programs and the local production. So let me shift now into a bit of a product focus and talk about some of the products, some of the blockbusters, I think, that are coming, that will drive some new opportunities and give you a sense of timing and the impact. And the first one that I'll get into is the fact that overall, our pipeline is as robust as it's ever been. That's more than we've ever had in our history and they cover a broad section of breeding advances, biotech advances, advances in information technology, as well as biological. That's clearly been the case in both the insect and the weed control technology. And this is really one of the first examples of using RNAi technology in an agricultural market and one of the first examples of a product that we'll launch. If I look a little bit further out in terms of technology, the next one I want to highlight is our Intacta technology. It was our biggest launch ever on 3 million acres, and we see this technology having a fit potentially on the 100 million-acre soybean opportunity that stretches across Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay. Intacta provides both the enhanced Roundup Ready 2 Yield technology, which means more yields for the grower, plus the Bt gene for controlling the insects and particularly the caterpillars, the loopers, the insects that have caused such a challenge for soybean production. It's turned out that this year, as you've read, there's been very severe insect pressure in South America and the performance of the products has been outstanding. These will bring, again, multiple modes of action for insect control to provide enhanced yield and durability and next-generation modes of action for weed control to, again, expand the product performance and give growers the benefit of that incremental lot and enhanced yield. Another one I'd highlight, which we're very excited in is the next generation product that will support our weed control platform, and that's the Roundup Ready Xtend system, where we combine the benefits of the Roundup technology and Roundup Ready with the opportunity to provide for specific tolerance to dicamba. We're making a lot of progress towards regulatory -- final regulatory approval in the U.S. and internationally. In fact, we've already gotten all the approvals from Canada. As you know, we're working to complete the Environmental Impact Statement with USDA and we expect that, depending on the timing of the final approval, we are in a position to be in the marketplace in 2015 with this technology. And then last point I'd highlight is we're moving the Xtend technology into multiple crops. So let me shift from specific products now to a couple of new platforms, and I'll talk about the BioAg Alliance with Novozymes. And I think it's poised for a lot of breakthroughs. But I think what the game change here is the fact that we're now able to supply new technology that makes the analysis and the screening and selection so much more effective. So I think the BioAg Alliance with Novozymes really creates a world-class capability in terms of microbe discovery, microbe testing, microbe production. The soil microbiota, the microbiome, is very different from field to field, and understanding that, being able to analyze that, compensate for it, is a big part of the opportunity. As we've noted consistently over the past years, the overall housing market has been generally defined by a rather large production deficit that has continued to grow over the past years. While questions have been raised as to the real normalized levels of production that are required to serve the U.S. current population, we believe that production levels in the 1 million to 1.2 million starts per year range are still too low for the needs of American household growth that is now normalizing. While measuring current production levels against historical norms of 1.5 million starts per year might be flawed logic as there may be a new normal, we believe that the very low inventory levels in existing and new homes, and the low vacancy rate and high and growing rental rates for apartments indicate that we are in short supply nationally. With that said, we believe that there continues to be a growing pent-up demand for dwellings of all types across the country, though stronger in some markets than others, and this demand will continue to propel a continued, long cycle, slow and steady market improvement. While demand has been constrained by limited access to mortgages, stronger general economic conditions, including lower unemployment, modest wage growth and general consumer confidence, are still driving consumers to form new households and to purchase homes and to rent apartments. We expect that demand will continue to build and come to the market over the next years, and that will drive increased production as the deficit in housing stock ultimately needs to be replenished. Nevertheless, land and labor shortages will continue to be limiting factors and will constrain supply and restrict the ability to quickly respond to growing demand, while the mortgage market and higher rents will continue to constrain that demand. We expect that these conditions will continue to result in a slow and steady positive homebuilding market and will enable slow, steady, though sometimes erratic, growth throughout the industry. This has been our consistent guiding theme over the past years, and we have mapped our strategy around this view. Each segment of our company has positioned itself for continued performance in 2016 and beyond, and we believe that we remain well positioned to execute our operating plans and strategies in each of these segments. Even with the somewhat erratic conditions that defined the early part of this year, we have remained resolute in our view that have generated our strategies. Our for-sale homebuilding operations experienced a healthy spring selling season with a sales pace of 3.9 sales per month per community. Our results reflect the slow but steady growth in the overall homebuilding market as our new home orders increased 10% year-over-year while community count grew 4% and our average sales price grew 4% to $362,000. Even while continued labor shortages and land and construction cost increases have tested our ability to match sales and delivery pace, our management team has carefully managed sales prices, maximized margins and focused on reducing SG&A to offset and maintain a strong net operating margin, which came in at 13.9%. As we've noted in past conference calls, we have adjusted our for-sale housing strategy as the recovery has matured and land pricing has adjusted to that recovery. There are 3 components of our core homebuilding segment strategy. They are: soft pivot, slower growth and focus on SG&A.\r\nTo begin, we've talked consistently about our soft pivot land strategy over the past years, away from the land-heavy acquisition strategy in the early stages of the recovery, and we're now targeting land acquisitions with a shorter 2- to 3-year average life. Second, we've noted in past quarter conference calls that given our now mature recovery, we have been and continue to carefully manage and limit our growth in order to grow the bottom line and to drive strong cash flow. We have moderated our top line growth targets to achieve a growth rate in the 7% to 10% range as we've redirected our management efforts towards maximizing our net operating margin. Third, with less pressure on the top line growth rate, we can intensify management focus on driving faster bottom line growth and cash flow by maximizing pricing power and using innovative strategies to drive our SG&A down. With demand growing steadily, land limited, labor tight and constrained mortgage availability, we believe that our three-pronged strategy for our homebuilding segment positions us well for this slow but steady growth environment. We feel that we can run our business at a steady and consistent growth rate with strong bottom line profitability and cash flow by measuring and changing our way to greater efficiency and performance in our core for-sale homebuilding segment. Moving on, our Financial Services group has had an outstanding second quarter as well. While the Financial Services operations have grown alongside our core homebuilding business, we've also benefited from a strong, though sometimes erratic, refi market as well as from the expansion of retail opportunities in both our mortgage and title platforms. Next, our Multifamily program continues to develop as a leading blue-chip developer of apartment communities across the country. The second quarter has continued an outstanding run for LMC, [COMPANY], which continues to complement our for-sale homebuilding operation. Since household formation has recovered at a slower rate than expected and many new households have been more inclined to rent than purchase, we have focused on building well-located rental communities to address this market opportunity. First-time home purchasers have come back to the market more slowly than they have historically and more slowly than expected. Our now almost $7 billion plus apartment strategy is proving to be very well timed as rental rates continue to climb and vacancies are at very low levels. Next, our Rialto segment continued to see challenges in the second quarter. While our Rialto segment continued to see challenges in the second quarter, we continue to see opportunity rising in our asset management business as we get closer to realizing the embedded value of our promote from our Rialto fund investments. Additionally, on a current basis, our fund and asset management business showed improved profitability over last year's second quarter, and we expect this trend to continue. Nevertheless, while Rialto Mortgage Finance was less of a contributor in the current period than in past quarters, we have been seeing sequential improvements in both volumes and margins for RMF, and the capital markets have generally healed, and we expect to improve -- improvement in contributions in the second half of the year. Overall, our Rialto platform enables us to invest across all real estate and financial products and allows us to capitalize on both short-term and long-term duration opportunities throughout the economic cycle. While the collapse of the capital markets in the beginning of the calendar year and the onetime write-off from a single asset negatively impacted year-to-date earnings for Rialto, this volatility has also created unique opportunities for new investments in our asset management business. The dysfunction in the financial market, along with new risk retention rules and banking regulations, will ultimately work to the benefit of Rialto's core competence in CMBS and financial products, and we will continue to grow as a best-in-class asset manager. And finally, as we noted in our press release, we've successfully completed an important step in the evolution of FivePoint, our strategic large-scale community builder. This transaction marks the next step in FivePoint's evolution as a strategic developer and manager of large-scale master-planned communities. It also marks a next step in [COMPANY]'s strategic mission to revert to our core homebuilding base. We feel very confident that our view of the market and the strategies that define our business segments have worked very well to position us for continued performance and future growth.", "I caution you that many statements on this call are forward-looking based on assumptions about the economy, world events, housing and financial markets, interest rates, the availability of labor and materials inflation and many other factors beyond our control that could significantly affect future results. As mortgage rates have stabilized and buyer confidence has improved, the increase in demand that began in January has continued through our second quarter and into the start of our third quarter. This improvement in demand, combined with our strategy of increasing our supply of spec homes into the spring selling season, and our focus on operational efficiency, has resulted in second quarter performance that well exceeded our guidance. As a result, we are raising our full year guidance across most metrics. Our homebuilding gross margin benefited from cost controls and greater leverage on fixed costs from higher homebuilding revenues. We are benefiting from approximately $50 million of cost reductions that we have taken over the past year, which we expect to be permanent savings, and we continue to target additional opportunities to become even more efficient. Although our second quarter contracts were down on a year-over-year basis, demand has improved significantly compared to the previous 3 quarters. As I pointed out in the past, there is a substantial shortage of homes for sale in the U.S. with housing starts failing to keep up with population growth, for at least the past 15 years. Now with 90% of outstanding mortgages under 5%, the market is seeing the further impact of a low interest rate lock-in effect, existing home buyers -- excuse me, existing homeowners are reluctant to give up their low rate mortgages, which has led to historically tight resale inventories. This phenomenon has become a boon for homebuilders and especially the larger, well-capitalized public builders who are more efficient and better positioned to take advantage of opportunities compared to smaller private builders. With such low levels of resale inventory on the market, buyers are gravitating to new homes. In addition to the underproduction of new homes in this country and the low level of resale inventory, there are many other factors that continue to support the housing market. These include favorable demographics with millions of millennials and baby boomers on the move. These trends have staying power that we believe will continue to support housing demand for years to come. A key part of our strategy heading into the spring selling season was to focus on increasing our supply of spec homes to support deliveries in the second half of fiscal '23 and throughout 2024. With demand better than expected this spring, this strategy is paying off. We believe that in this market, our spec strategy continues to make sense. With such limited resale inventory, specs fill a significant gap in supply. The improvement in cycle times, combined with a stronger demand environment and our focus on increasing spec production has led us to increase our full year deliveries guidance. We now expect to deliver between 8,900 and 9,500 homes, an increase of approximately 700 homes at the midpoint of our previous guidance. We are also increasing our guidance for our full year average delivered price to between $975,000 and $995,000. We are also increasing our full year adjusted gross margin guidance from 27% to 27.8%. As I mentioned earlier, we expect to benefit from greater fixed cost leverage on higher revenues. On the land front, we remain committed to our disciplined and capital-efficient land acquisition strategy as well as our focus on returning capital to stakeholders. Our financial position and liquidity remain very strong. These actions reflect our confidence in the business and our commitment to delivering returns to shareholders."]

Name: 30_security_cloud_firewall_wan
Representative_Docs: ["The events of 2020 have underscored how transformative technology can be to help adapt, innovate and increase productivity. Cybercrime continues to accelerate as the explosion of data and devices have expanded the attack surface, and the shift to work from home has required additional cybersecurity controls and operational changes. These same events have created an opportunity for cyber criminals to exploit and capitalize on the expanding number of vulnerabilities. Our recently published incident response report highlighted increased risk areas in direct response to the pandemic. These included an increased risk with more people accessing SaaS applications, delays in vulnerability patching, circumvention of VPN connections and increased phishing attacks. This is the first time we've seen cyber criminals globally focus on one issue, with threat actors using COVID-19-themed tactics to exploit vulnerabilities. For many years, the security industry has been overrun with thousands of point products that do not enable organizations to mount a holistic defense against adversaries whose unrelenting attacks only have to succeed once. Through a variety of means, the adversary has consistently been able to navigate between security controls, going undetected and undeterred in organizations that lack integrated detection and response capabilities across their environment. We believe that the ability to outpace the adversary at scale requires an integrated security platform that closes the gaps between point products, puts security detections in context of risk to an organization and automates the remediation process with agility. Our superior threat detection and remediation capabilities are accelerated with deep learning, machine learning and workflow automation to detect security risk to an organization quickly with high fidelity, and to reduce both assessorial dwell time and mean time to remediate. Our cloud-native platform takes a different approach, building on our expertise as a global leader in managed security over the last 20 years, because we fundamentally believe that the only way to win this fight is through the combined power of the community working together. Because the adversaries work together, albeit in a mercenary way, increasingly leveraging the same data science and technology capabilities that the security industry does. Our integrated, inclusive, holistic approach continues to gain momentum by allowing customers to: One, detect and respond to threats across the complete environment, including endpoints, network, business systems and cloud infrastructures regardless of the underlying point product technologies; two, provide accurate and prioritize insights through automated asset discovery and classification, vulnerability assessment and risk prioritization; three, leverage our deep security operations expertise to automate and simplify investigations, orchestrate and automate responses and workflows and enable collaboration across security and IT functions in a single platform that sits at the heart of their security operations. Our holistic approach means customers benefit from the capabilities of our platform without having to rip and replace existing point products nor shift to a single-vendor ecosystem. We also see a near-term future where what are now individual security product markets, such as SOAR, SIEM, vulnerability management and more, increasingly become integrated features or capabilities of a holistic security analytics platform. And as this trend continues, I believe we are well positioned to be successful in the emerging XDR market that anticipates convergence across historically stand-alone technology segments. In Q3, we continued to focus on our software products and our transformation. In Q3, we continued to make great progress in expanding our go-to-market efforts, focusing on customer success and attracting new logos to our cloud-native platform. One such new customer example, a global European chemicals company with operations in more than 100 countries, was seeking a security partner to focus on threat detection and response. They purchased our TDR software to give them a unified approach to managing their security program with holistic detection and automated investigation capabilities across endpoints, networks and cloud activity in a single dashboard. Another new customer is a privately held video streaming company in North America that focuses on live, customizable e-commerce applications. The company desired a security solution to help minimize risk and establish confidence and trust. They chose our new VDP product because of its simplicity to get up and running quickly, and automation of the vulnerability management and prioritization processes, which provides substantial time and resource savings. In addition, as the historical leader in the MSSP market, we believe there is new and compelling opportunity for us to scale our cloud-native software platform that enables a broader community of managed security service providers, allowing a growing community access to our software analytics and expertise, accelerating the adoption of our cloud-native platform and, as a community, to combat the adversary at scale. Core to all we do is customer success. I talked a moment ago about the progress we are making in attracting new customers to our platform. For example, in North America, a $2 billion manufacturing company was looking for a security partner that could provide visibility and controls to reduce their cybersecurity risk. They also used our built-in real-time chat to collaborate with our threat experts during live investigations. They appreciated how TDR provides their leadership with the latest threat intelligence insights and research from our counterthreat unit to meet the dynamic changes in cybersecurity and inform their overall security strategy. In each of these examples, customers benefited from having full visibility of their security environment with technology solutions that work together to protect their business. We've made great progress in extending our portfolio, adding another application and more capabilities to increase differentiated value for our customers. We recently announced significant feature enhancements to TDR with the addition of log management and search and reporting capabilities for users to have an integrated, contemporary alternative to traditional SIEMs. Our VDP product provides contextual awareness to vulnerabilities with an ML-driven prioritization engine to focus on the highest risk to an organization. We are transforming our business to strengthen the security community and beat the adversary at scale. We have taken over 20 years of security operations experience, threat intelligence and technological advancements to reimagine how security should be done. This is a multiyear journey, and we will continue to focus our transformation on expanding our go-to-market, advancing the delivery of our cloud-native platform and ensuring the success of our community, customers and partners to be a force for good.", "We believe that customer recognition of the exceptional value proposition we provided by a high performance for the ASIC technology and integrate FortiOS. Product revenue growth was very strong at 39%, extending our position as a product revenue leader in the cybersecurity industry. Our product revenue performance reflects the strong demand we have built over the past 18 months across our security solutions along with the successful execution of our internal team in managing the supply chain challenges. 3 growth drivers, the heightened threat environment, the convergence of security and networking and the consolidation of security functionality and vendors together with the opportunity to upsell additional security services to a significant installed base are expected to drive future growth. First, the threat landscape, including ransomware, continue to expand an evolving targeting company of our size, location and industries. To counter the threat landscape, we are implementing a unique universal ZTNA across a wide range of customers, driving triple-digit growth for this product and delivering a comprehensive approach to zero trust that is consistent for any user anywhere on any device and supporting today's hybrid workforce. Second, for years, [PERSON] has lead strategy around convergence of networking and security. We estimate the total addressable market for networking and security will increase from $54 billion today to $73 billion in 2026. Convergence accelerate digital transformation and substantially reduce our operation costs and combining networking modernization with dynamic security not [Indiscernible] spend every part of the network, especially now that many companies are merging SOC and IOC operation together. [PERSON] is leading the convergence trend with a wide range of technologies, including network firewall segmentation, Secure SD-WAN, OT security and 5G in a single operation system, which can be deployed as hardware, software, cloud and as a service. Fortinet continues to gain Secure SD-WAN market share as our integrated Secure SD-WAN solution delivers better security, performance and efficiency over more traditional offerings. We believe we can achieve #1 market share in SD-WAN in the next couple of years. Our third growth driver is the consolidation of our vendors and product functionality with FortiASIC huge computing power advantage, FortiOS can integrate most security function than our competitors, together with over 30 key products ranging from endpoint to network to the cloud security, [PERSON] provides our customer with easier operation while lower the management cost and the total cost of ownership. Additionally, we are very focused on upselling value-added security services to a significant customer base. This leadership position and the substantial installed base creates attractive economy of scale and an opportunity to upsell additional security services.", '[PERSON], I think, listen, our goal wasn\'t to just buy an EDR vendor. First off, it was fleshing out this entire security strategy where we\'ve actually gotten started with network security. So almost, like if you could have a pieced together 5, 7 years ago, Symantec and Palo Alto in one, that\'s what kind of we were trying to do in these first 2 markets, network and endpoint. And it was always a mystery to me, why was it the network security people didn\'t get endpoint security, and the endpoint security people didn\'t get network. These were to separate, but they\'re left and right hand because the threat vector could come in from any of these points. And we\'ve seen the network security companies do fairly well. And we felt like we could -- we had a really good presence, tens of millions of endpoints of Workspace ONE, but we didn\'t do security. And customers came to us and said, "Listen, you\'re managing these laptops, tablets, phones with Workspace ONE, but you don\'t do all of the security, antivirus, EDR, audit remediation and vulnerability management on and on, kind of the traditional Symantec-type suite. First off, here is 30%, 40% more R&D, go and build what Symantec built, but in the cloud, okay? Unify Workspace ONE and Carbon Black so a single agent can manage and secure laptops, never been done before. Secondly, on the server side, typically, these endpoint security folks never really cared about a workload. We are a server company. We have 85 million servers that we virtualize with workloads of vSphere, let\'s get Carbon Black inside the hypervisor and make it agentless. So we thought about that even prior to the Carbon Black acquisition. We feel very good about endpoint and workload security disrupting the older players. They\'re all respected companies, Symantec, McAfee Trend and others, but we feel there\'s a more modern way to get this done in a more cloud-native, thin sensor and a focus on both endpoint and workload security. And then the final thing we see as tremendous synergy points between what we do in network security, data center networking, firewalls, load balances, SD-WAN, when we do an endpoint and workload security, including Workspace ONE and Carbon Black and then the new areas of cloud security, we\'re generating all this telemetry, okay? So you\'re going to see us increasingly drive security analytics to be extended detection and response, okay, and that\'s a game changer.']

Name: 31_commerce_stores_store_online
Representative_Docs: ["I just want to start my presentation with a little color on our updated guidance we release this past Monday. Warm weather in November gave way to a very promotional environment on and off the mall. However, we believe, with more seasonal weather patterns, we would experience a stronger, more profitable December and January. This left us with a dilemma, either become more promotional to drive customers into our store or face an inventory issue on seasonal product. We chose to focus on inventory control across all categories, which resulted in improved self-performance but at the cost of margin. We have an -- we have incredible systems, which allow our stores and merchants teams to tailor merchandise and promotions by location. We are a growth story. We currently operate in only 35 states with unparalleled growth opportunities. Over the past 4 years, we have expanded our digital presence across all mediums but still have long runway for growth. Our customer is extremely loyal and loves the broad assortment of footwear for the family that our stores offer. Brick-and-mortar stores need to stay relevant and offer the customers a unique shopping experience in order for -- in order to effectively compete today. We believe our stores -- the size of our stores allow us to offer a customer a unique shopping experience. So this past year, we started experimenting with shop-in-shop formats. We took what was -- since our customer is primarily a blue-collar consumer, and work shoes is a very large part of our overall business, we took 37 stores, and we put in a work shoe shop, so we become a destination shop for work. We believe that it sets us apart from our competition and allows us to take the world's #1 brand and become the destination store and a family channel for that brand. Now I'd like to talk about our marketing program for just a minute. The cornerstone of our marketing strategy is our loyalty program. While we remain committed to acquiring additional new members, we now are transitioning to managing our loyalty members more effectively. Our initial goal in managing our loyalty members more effectively revolves around segmenting customer data for marketing and real estate purposes. However, we have learned that a large percentage of our customers are higher income than we previously thought, and that baby boomers truly are devout Shoe Carnival customers. We fully expect to maintain a 30% year-over-year growth over the next 3 years. We continue to be focused on mobile where, during peak periods, we have seen more than 40% of our online revenue come from mobile devices. We will shift our marketing investments into digital marketing, as more and more customers are disconnecting from the landlines, from traditional newsprint and from cable and satellite. Several years ago, we began to utilize our stores as shipping points for our multichannel initiatives. Our customers love the service they receive -- on their purchase, which they receive approximately 2 days after they place their buy. A couple of months ago, we launched the buy online, ship to store and pick up in store. We're very, very pleased with the performance of this initiative and expect, long term, it will give us ability to reduce shipping cost. Next up will be vendor drop-ship, which will allow our -- us to utilize, seamless to our customer, a vendor's inventory to expand our selection. We believe we have a proven concept to grow into all 50 states. Remember that, through our multichannel initiatives, we can offer the customers, even in our smallest store and a smallest market, a product assortment that spans our entire product selection. This map spells out the opportunity for growth in the United States and all markets. Our real estate software program looks at a typical Shoe Carnival customer, identifies where they live and then pinpoints the best area to open a store. So we're very excited about the mid-market and small market opportunity. In summary, we believe that Shoe Carnival offers our customer a unique shopping experience, compelling value with fun and exciting shopping experience. Most importantly, Shoe Carnival has a long runway for growth.", "Despite a challenging macro environment, the team executed and we made progress advancing our various strategic initiatives. For the first quarter, constant currency sales increased nearly 8% or about $11 billion with strength across all segments. We continue to gain share and grow unit volume in grocery. At the headline level, consumer spending has proven resilient. But below the surface, we continue to see signs that customers remain choiceful, particularly in discretionary categories. In addition to the persistence of inflation in food and consumables, customers were also impacted by a reduction of SNAP benefits and lower tax refunds. Many of the same impacts on consumer spending in the U.S. affected our international markets, too. Headline inflation in food and consumables came down over 400 basis points from the start of Q1 to the end of the quarter, but prices remain high, and customers are being cautious with their spend in discretionary categories. We expect category mix to remain a gross margin headwind for the balance of FY '24. The higher-margin initiatives that are connected to our core omni retail business, including marketplace, advertising and membership continue to meaningfully outgrow the base. Our global advertising business delivered strong growth of over 30% in Q1. In the U.S., Walmart Connect advertising sales increased nearly 40% as we experienced strong momentum in new advertisers, particularly from marketplace sellers. Advertisers are responding to our recently launched in-club sales attribution feature, which provides advertisers with clear insights on the returns of digital ad spend, both online and in clubs, while enhancing member experience. Members spend more than nonmembers. Turning back to the middle of the P&L. SG&A expenses leveraged 58 basis points, aided by strong sales growth across the enterprise, a continued focus on managing costs into moderating sales growth as inflation lessens and lapping some COVID-related wage costs in the U.S. last year. The team continued to do a good job managing inventory, and we ended the quarter down 7%, including a more than 9% decline in [COMPANY] cost and inventory are two of the key controllables as we navigate an uncertain macro environment. Let me take a moment to discuss our returns or specifically return on investment or ROI, which declined by 120 basis points this quarter. At our Investor Day in April, I said that we want our ROI to go up every year, and I still believe that will be the case this year. For Walmart U.S., comp sales were strong, up 7.4%, reflecting higher store traffic trends as well as strong growth in store-fulfilled pickup and delivery. From a category perspective, comp sales were driven by strong growth in food and health and wellness, partially offset by a decline in general merchandise sales. Share gains in grocery continued, including from higher income households as our strong price gaps resonate with customers who are increasingly prioritizing value and convenience. In this environment, as customers manage household budgets more tightly and are biasing spending toward everyday essentials, we're reinforcing our value proposition across the merchandise offering, including seasonal event savings featuring high-quality owned brands and leaning into opening price points. E-commerce sales were led by continued double-digit growth in store-fulfilled pickup and delivery. Strong flow-through on higher sales contributed to SG&A expense leverage, which offset gross profit pressure, resulting in strong operating income growth of 11.7% relative to comp sales growth of 7.4%. Our International segment delivered an outstanding quarter with strong growth in both sales and profit, continuing the momentum built in the back half of last year. Impressively, operating income grew more than 3x faster than sales, up 41%, with each market delivering year-over-year improvement. The strong profit flow-through is particularly encouraging as the team has been delivering operating efficiencies on top of strong sales growth. It's clear, our omni model is resonating with customers across income demographics who are seeking out [COMPANY] digitally and in stores, curbside and via delivery. As we continue to scale digital capabilities in our markets around the world, we have an opportunity to drive significant growth in the top line over the coming years. In addition, as I mentioned earlier, we're making progress in improving our business mix as we scale a portfolio of highly attractive growth initiatives that reinforce our core retail model and will directly reshape our e-commerce and enterprise profit trajectory. Over time, we expect revenue growth across a diversified set of drivers, improved category mix and increasingly accretive business mix, coupled with improved unit economics. This is all fueled by supply chain investments with attractive payback cycles. Turning to guidance. There continues to be a great deal of uncertainty looking out over the balance of this year as macro pressures on the consumer have gradually intensified. As such, we continue to maintain a prudent approach to our outlook while, at the same time, having a high level of confidence in what we can control. We're raising our full year guidance to reflect Q1 performance and our expectations for Q2. Our expectations are for Walmart U.S. and International to grow slightly faster than our prior view, and for [PERSON]'s Club growth to be consistent with our February guidance. We expect operating income in constant currency to increase approximately 4% to 4.5%, including an expected 100 basis point impact from LIFO charges. If the consumer environment tightens further, we have a compelling value proposition with everyday low prices and a suite of conveniences to continue to gain wallet share. And the transformation of our business mix toward higher-margin streams of value is underway, helping to protect our profits today and to drive better profit growth in the future.", "[PERSON] brings with her excellent experience and expertise, with more than 25 years as a financial professional in the consumer products arena. He has been a great partner and advocate of [COMPANY], playing a pivotal role in helping transform the company during his tenure. With the philosophy of financial conservatism and discipline, [PERSON] leaves us in an excellent financial position, one that will enable us to invest in our future and weather inevitable economic cycles. On the product side, Power continues to be a growing category, and our Duo line is outpacing expectation, already becoming a significant collection. Urban Attitudes has been a very -- has been very successful for us over the past few years, and this refreshed collection was well received by dealers. Our new innovation center at our Dayton, Tennessee campus is scheduled to open this summer and is a testament to our commitment to remain the industry's most innovative manufacturer. This helps keep the [COMPANY] name at the forefront in consumers' minds when they think about furniture that is not only great-looking and comfortable but offers all the bells and whistles they want. This process will be supported by the new innovation center, where our engineering and manufacturing teams are working side-by-side to develop, test, refine and bring exciting and progressive new products, like Duo, to the market. And as our sales and marketing teams worked to drive sales across all product category and channels, we will also benefit as we gain further traction with Duo, renewed interest in Urban Attitudes and momentum with other product categories, we will be able to further leverage the fixed-cost structure of our plants with the additional volume. Last summer, we unveiled an e-commerce strategy that includes 3 components, with the first to sell more [COMPANY] furniture online. While many [COMPANY] consumers seem to prefer to shop in a retail outlet, one of our objectives is to increase sales with younger customers, many of whom prefer to shop online. And finally, we are investing in early-stage furniture brands and companies with strong business models and a focus on selling directly to consumers online. While e-commerce is a small part of our business today, we believe it has the potential to play a more significant role in the future. The La-Z-Boy Furniture Galleries store system is vibrant and growing and is a key element of our expansive strategy, and the company, along with our independent dealer base, will continue to open stores in pursuit of the 400-store target. Our objective continues to be to build a $1.6 billion retail business through the store network, and we believe we can achieve that level over time with our improved store performance, even if we have fewer stores than our original plan. We are very pleased with the trajectory of our case goods business, which is well positioned for growth and market share gains as it continues to leverage supply chain excellence and domestic distribution capabilities to provide the excellent service to our customers with beautifully designed collections. While most of you are very familiar with our integrated retail strategy, some of you on today's call may be new to our story, so the benefit of this strategy bears repeating. Sales through our company-owned La-Z-Boy Furniture Galleries stores provide the company with the greatest level of profitability, due to our integrated retail model, where we benefit from the combined margin, earning a profit on both the wholesale and retail sales at the same time. Name: 32_students_education_student_school
Representative_Docs: ["[PERSON] had a strong third quarter, exceeding both our top and bottom line expectations, with Chegg Services revenue growing 8% year-over-year, reaching 4.8 million subscribers. Our results reflect excellent execution and show the inherent profitability of our model while continuing to invest in future growth. We regularly monitor the trends in education. What has changed is that students are increasingly going to schools offering online and hybrid classes, which are now offered by over half of the U.S. higher education institutions. We believe these trends are all positive for [PERSON]. We continue to make investments to increase the value of [PERSON]'s offerings, both to our existing students as well as expand the opportunity to reach new learners. In addition to providing academic support, we are also adding nonacademic services and job skills preparation, which we believe will expand our TAM, increase retention, increase ARPU and better serve students. We believe this is a major opportunity, which is why we recently announced the promotion of [PERSON] to Chief Operating Officer. Our strategy continues to be to increase our TAM as well as the percentage of students who subscribe to [COMPANY]. This increases our ARPU and profitability and most importantly, serves the students better. As we add more value, we expect to add more students, which is why we continue to invest in more forms of content, subjects and personalization. As an example, our investment in Uversity, which was recently made available to students, is performing well, allowing us to better target the exact learning content students want. In addition to Uversity, our plan is to expand value by adding nonacademic services and job skills preparation in the future. Internationally, we are prioritizing market share growth by delivering compelling value propositions for students in their countries, increasing our subscriber base through local pricing, content and user experience. These efforts are focused on expanding our reach in major markets, including Turkey, where we recently launched a fully localized app and have seen a significant increase in downloads, activation and engagement. We also just launched our Spanish language app in beta, and we believe this will be a major opportunity for us going forward. Students' needs continue to evolve, including the growth in demand for language learning. With over half of U.S. students reporting wanting to learn another language, we see a tremendous opportunity for U.S. growth. Our partnership with [PERSON] continues to yield excellent results. And as they grow their customer base among large employers, we are seeing increased adoption of our courses as well as a very strong learner completion rate, which is how we are measured for quality and value.", "The past few years have brought change and disruption to how people live, work, entertain and learn, among other things. There is no doubt to me, however, as these challenges and opportunities present themselves, core primary education will remain key to our society. The latest disruption seems to be generative AI and how it will change every aspect of our lives and all facets of the economy, including education. But we must also recognize that change is a constant, and I believe the best organizations embrace change. I believe that this iteration of change will have a massive impact on our industry. First and foremost, I think we need to appreciate that K-12 education as we know it today will not be going away anytime soon. In fact, I think AI has the ability to transform K-12 education in a very positive way that will enable our students to accelerate and personalize their learning in ways we have dreamed about but not really achieved previously. For example, when we consider the training and education required to become a computer engineer, well, maybe we should be teaching some of those skills in high school, but not in terms of computer programming, but instead in terms of navigating the functional output of the code that AI will provide for them. Since Stride was founded over 20 years ago, it has been at the forefront of personalized learning for students. And AI has the ability to personalize student feedback, assessments and content at the individual level like nothing before. AI-powered content can provide customized lessons to students based on their learning style and free up teachers to spend more time with students and less time on administrative tasks. And giving teachers more time to actually teach will allow them to spend individual time with students and provide a human connection. The relationships that teachers build with students are incredibly important for student outcomes, and AI-powered learning will allow those to flourish. Ultimately, I believe that giving teachers an incredible AI toolkit will be beneficial for both students and teachers. The landscape of AI is quickly evolving, and we want to be sure to take a measured and long-term approach and not just hop on the bandwagon for headline's sake. Our job will be to ensure that we provide interactive learning experiences that build up the durable skills students will need to adapt to the evolving demands of the marketplace. Ensuring we prepare students with the skills they can take with them through their entire careers is incredibly important. We've already been applying AI internally to supplement many of the ongoing efficiency efforts we've talked about before. We believe we can continue to increase productivity and automate many of the routine administrative tasks for both teachers and corporate employees. We will also continue to improve the user experience with AI-powered chatbots while removing friction in our admission and enrollment funnel. It should also allow us to generate content, from assessments to practice materials to full courses, much faster than previously. We will begin to roll out additional personalized learning tools to further strengthen student outcomes. We can use AI-powered programs to track progress and intervene earlier when a student is struggling. This will allow us to provide personalized learning at greater scale and real time, resulting in stronger student outcomes. Teachers will remain core to our offerings. While AI is good at following instructions and completing tasks, you need teachers to foster creativity and develop critical thinking skills. Teachers can encourage students to explore new ideas, solve problems, use data, create models and provide mentorship in ways AI cannot. For a company that is growing near double digits for multiple years, has a very attractive future growth profile and TAM, we believe that is a fairly low multiple and represents a great value. These results reinforce our belief that families view us as an option when they feel like their current school's not delivering what they need. And increasingly, families now recognize that they have a choice when it comes to their child's education and they are choosing us. It shows that our efforts are translating to a more satisfied customer. And all of these metrics indicate we are delivering for our customers, and they have led to improving in-year retention, which is at its highest level ever. On top of all the accolades we receive, we continue to launch innovative partnerships and programs across our schools. We deepened our relationship with Southern New Hampshire University to lower the cost of tuition for graduates of eligible Stride-powered programs. Additionally, our strong in-year enrollment and retention in fiscal year '23 means that we finished the year in a good position to retain students for the upcoming school year. Given this data, we are well positioned to return to enrollment growth for the first time since the pandemic. And when I became CEO, I said my #1 goal is to ensure we grow every year, and I believe we are currently on track to do so. We are here to embrace change and innovation. We want to disrupt the status quo. Stride can change the future.", "$ years ago, [COMPANY] went public, viewed as a textbook rental company, as nearly all our revenue came from print textbooks. But even then we had a much bigger vision: to serve the modern generation of students by building an all-digital education platform. We saw a huge $1 trillion education industry, representing 7% of the GDP, and that 15% of the U.S. population was participating in on an annual basis. At the same time, it was an industry that was experiencing significant pressure, was cutting investment and was increasingly misaligned with its customer. We understood that even though today's students were more diverse than ever, they all had been raised on technology and the Internet. We saw more students on their own with little or no learning support who were taking on huge amounts of debt, taking longer to graduate--if they graduated at all--and failing to find jobs that were worthy of a degree. To address this, we have been building a platform of interconnected learning services that focuses on helping students pick their classes, get better grades, master their subjects, pass their classes and then start their career, delivering all of our services in the manner students expect: online, on-demand, adaptive, personalized, affordable and, of course, all backed by human help. Our key services--Chegg Study, Tutors and Writing--are all high-quality, low-cost learning services that address students' biggest pain point, and [COMPANY] is becoming the brand students turn to for help as the industry undergoes massive and rapid disruption. What's becoming clear to us is the more we invest in solving students' biggest pain points with more content, capabilities and format, the bigger the opportunity gets for [COMPANY]. The depth and breadth of our learning material has created a giant competitive mode, and we believe Chegg Study is now considered indispensable for an increasing number of college students. As powerful as Chegg Study is already, we believe the service will become even more relevant to an increasing TAM as we continue to expand its content and capability. To that end, we recently announced the acquisition of Cogeon, the developer of app MATH 42, and adapted AI-driven math application, which has been downloaded, which has been downloaded over 2 million times. Math is a universal need and, unfortunately, a universal problems, as 64% of U.S. students are not prepared for college-level math, and over 40% of U.S. students take at least 1 remedial math course. Adding this technology into our suite of products has applications not only for primary path subjects, but also across every discipline in STEM. We couldn't be more excited about adding math to [COMPANY]'s suite of services, and we believe it will deepen our relationship with existing subscribers and extent our reach into new audiences like high school. Even as students look to AI-driven tools to help augment their learning, we know that one-on-one human help will continue to be critical in the learning process, which is why we continue to invest in Chegg Tutors. Our extensive network of human experts allows students to learn on their own time with educators in whatever subject they need help with. The power of our interconnected platform is evident as more than half of our Chegg Tutor customers come from other [COMPANY] services. [COMPANY]'s direct-to-student model is becoming not only big, but also what we believe is the most efficient way to teach and reach students at scale with high-William Logan, low-cost learning products. Our philosophy of online, on-demand, personalized and adaptive services backed by human help has attracted millions of students, and our transformation to an all-digital business model has created increased value for our students and our shareholders. As we continue to grow and drive needed change in the education industry, we believe we will be one of the most valuable resources for students, parents and educators and employers in one of the most important stages of a student's life."]

Name: 33_theaters_movie_films_movies
Representative_Docs: ["The movies that go to PVOD at 17 days are going to stay in theaters, and we expect to still sell a whole bunch of tickets at our theaters even when movies are available on PVOD. Our company has invested billions of dollars over the past few years to make sure that our theaters are in great condition, and that our fleet of theaters appeals to consumers. Similarly, I'll remind everybody the conventional wisdom about streaming and PVOD and all this before the pandemic was -- by the way, conventional wisdom from people who I disagree with but that's a different issue -- was oh, theaters are an anachronism, why would anybody go to a theater? And so movies aren't going to get pulled from theaters. On the issue of when people find out that a film will be going to PVOD, remember that not all films will. So already you've unpredictability as to which films are going to go PVOD and which films are not going to go PVOD, especially if some other studios take very few films to PVOD, and even Universal itself has said that on many of their films, they won't go to the home in 17 days. And there's been enormous discussion and pressure within the industry over the past 4 or 5 years to bring those windows forward. Those windows have been fully protected under the terms of the Universal agreement.", "I intend to take the next few minutes today to provide you with a high level review of our results for the third quarter but focus the majority of my formal remarks updating you on the progress we've made at AMC on the key priorities that we outlined on our last earnings call in early August as well as announce new initiatives you'll be hearing about for the first time. On our last call in early August, I remarked that Q3 would be no picnic, and that prediction was spot on. You are already aware of the softness of the third quarter industry box office in North America with fewer big movies, fewer wide releases and several movies that did not resonate with audiences, leading to an industry-wide 14% decline in the U.S. and Canadian box office, the most difficult third quarter in about a decade. But there were also 2 industry-wide bright spots. Second, hundreds have been arguing that teens and millennials are shunning theaters for mobile devices, but a recent Forbes article and Piper Jaffray survey both concluded that, in reality, teens and millennials are increasingly more likely to see movies at theaters because of the better immersive experiences now being offered like those provided by AMC's luxurious recliners; reserved seating options; unique food and beverage menus; for those 21 and above, our almost 270 MacGuffins bars; and for all moviegoers, our approximately 270 IMAX Dolby Cinema and PRIME at AMC premium large-format sight and sound U.S. auditoriums. As a high fixed cost, low variable cost business, our performance by definition will be less than inspiring in an environment where industry-wide revenues are declining by double digits. Having said that, we are encouraged that for the third quarter AMC exceeded consensus analyst estimates for revenue, for adjusted EBITDA and for diluted EPS. We're also pleased that in so many fronts we outperformed the industry. That our entire domestic circuit did well reflects that we made real progress in both the AMC and Carmike circuits. But within the legacy AMC circuit, as you look through our Q3 operating metrics, we are pleased that you'll see data point after data point after data point where AMC outperformed the industry and our principal competition. We're especially pleased too with our performance as the largest European exhibitor with theaters in 14 countries. With a similar slate of Hollywood movies that we had in the U.S., pro forma third quarter 2017 versus pro forma 2016, European revenues were down less than 1%, much better than in the U.S. and adjusted EBITDA actually increased by about 1% with adjusted EBITDA margins up slightly year-over-year but up significantly when compared to Q2 of 2017. We expect moviegoing through year-end will be robust. The evidence simply does not speak to a secular decline in our industry. There were some tough months in 2017 but the trend looking backwards and our forecast looking forwards lead us to be highly optimistic. To the contrary of the thesis of secular decline, domestic movie theaters in the U.S. and Canada right now sell more than 1.2 billion movie theater tickets each year. Item 2, we continue to work diligently to improve operations at the former Carmike theaters, and we expect that the actions we've already taken are paying some dividends now in the fourth quarter. I'm pleased to report that after much dedicated effort this year, we are seeing that the Carmike ship is on a clear path to being righted. We've already taken many actions on the Carmike circuit: rebranding the theaters; reconcepting many of the theaters; improving the food and beverage product across all the theaters; addressing deferred maintenance issues; signing up new loyalty program members in droves; benefiting from a more functional, attractive website and app; repricing many of the Carmike theaters; and training all the local theater management teams. Like for like, Carmike theaters are now performing exactly like comparable AMC Theatres. Similarly, the market share changes of the AMC and Carmike theaters that were not equipped with recliner seats also were identical. So that's the next major step, and that's why we picked up the pace on identifying the best opportunities to renovate theaters in the Carmike circuit full AMC style with recliner seating. Item 3, Europe, Europe, Europe and Europe. By next week, 3 Odeon theaters will have completed recliner renovations. By year-end 2018, we will have at least 25 Odeon theaters equipped with recliner seats, including arguably the most prestigious theater in all of Europe, the almost 2,000-seat Odeon Leicester Square. The very early results are stunning, comparable to the early attendance gains and returns we witnessed when we introduced recliners in the United States 6 years ago. And for those of you who have been wondering where we could generate growth in our Nordic Cinemas acquisition, in 2018, Nordic will add 7 new-build theaters across Scandinavia and the Baltics. In 2018, we now anticipate adding approximately 10 new-build theaters and spot acquisitions in the United States and adding 12 new-build theaters and spot acquisitions in Europe, 22 new theaters in total for AMC globally. But importantly for us, in 2018, we also expect to renovate about 55 theaters, about the same number as in each of 2016 and 2017 but in 2018, with 1/3 of those projects being in Europe and 2/3 in the United States. We did institute a $30 million profit improvement program, a small portion of which was reflected in our Q3 results and which will continue to kick in during the fourth quarter. Showing that we already are seeing some improvement sequentially compared to the second quarter of 2017, in Q3, adjusted EBITDA margins in the U.S. remained exactly flat with Q2 despite a $61.7 million decrease in revenues, indicating that we did a better job adjusting our expenses to our revenues in Q3 than was the case in Q2. We also expect that margins will continue to rise in the fourth quarter of 2017 as our revenues rise and as we still tightly manage our costs. To strengthen our liquidity position and to put us in a position to delever, in August, we told you that we turned on a dime and had reduced our CapEx plan for 2017 and 2018 by some $200 million. Especially with the encouraging early returns for European theater renovations, we are currently seriously exploring the idea of an IPO of our European theaters on the London Stock Exchange sometime between July of 2018 and April of 2019. That could generate multi hundreds of millions of dollars of cash for AMC, which could either be used by AMC to delever or to return cash to shareholders as we would decide at that time based on the then current circumstances. In September, we announced an investment in virtual reality through Dreamscape Immersive and our plan to launch 6 Dreamscape locations at or near our U.S. and U.K. theaters by 2019 in addition to our currently envisioned IMAX VR deployments. We think virtual reality done well at our theaters could be an intriguing traffic generator. For some considerable time, we have been predicting weakness in the third quarter and through box office due to the quantity and subject matter of the films that were scheduled to be released. At the same time, however, we consistently have been bullish about the fourth quarter movie slate. When Hollywood and international moviemakers offer appealing movies, Americans and Europeans will pour into our theaters in huge numbers and pay top dollar to do so. We believe that the naysaying arising from the May, July, August and October box office is misplaced, especially coming immediately after 2.5 years of record box office performance and just before what we expect will be strong and robust consumer demand throughout year-end. Accordingly in our opinion, those bearish investors who have been doubting the viability and strength of the movie industry generally, the movie theater industry generally and of AMC specifically, are betting the wrong way. We could not be more optimistic about our ability to deliver strong financial results in the coming years.", "I think long term, the -- we've always believed that there is a segment of the population out there going, and there's a segment of the population out there that just doesn't go to movie theaters. And this structure with AMC allows us to take advantage of people who do go to movie theaters, 17 days of exclusivity at minimum for theaters. But very soon after in the same marketing window, we can tap into that very large audience that doesn't go to movie theaters and right now is just going to SVOD to watch movies. So we think the structure allows us to tap into that incremental revenue stream, allowing AMC to share in a little bit and other exhibitors, and at the same time, preserve that theatrical window, which is so critical to the film business. We still need theatrical and need different business models in other markets. Shorter term, one of the implications of this, I'm hoping, is that we currently are stuck in a bit of a chicken-and-the-egg situation in the theatrical business, where movie studios like ours don't want to release movies into theaters when we will have only a smattering of theaters open. We need a pretty robust amount of theaters open to justify our spend. So we think this model will actually allow movies to come back to theaters when it's safe a lot more quickly than they would have in the current environment."]

Representative_Docs: ["We've taken a strategy that, to an extent, capitalizes on what's happening in China in a secular way. Obviously, a high growth helps, but this is not where our game plan is at. And then I think, ultimately, thematically, we're right over the target on where the Chinese government is investing. The move from coal to gas is going to be enormous over the next 10 or 15 years. So I think we're in the right businesses with the right team on the ground and the right relationships in country and -- where we operate as a Chinese company in China.", "I think that it's by design.
